question: Which tiger reserve in the South Division launched the “Vanjeevi Didi” initiative in February 2026?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Palamu Tiger Reserve**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• The **Vanjeevi Didi** initiative was officially launched in the **South Division** of the **Palamu Tiger Reserve (PTR)** in **February 2026** to strengthen community-based conservation.

• This program specifically recruits and trains **local women** from forest-fringe villages to act as **Vanjeevi Didis** (Sisters of the Forest), serving as a vital link between the **Forest Department** and the local population.

• The primary roles of these women include monitoring **forest fires**, reporting **illegal grazing** or **poaching activities**, and educating villagers on **wildlife conservation**.

• The initiative is designed to mitigate **man-animal conflict** by providing early warnings and fostering a sense of **ownership** and **stewardship** among the local tribal communities.

• By formalizing the role of women in **biodiversity management**, the project provides **sustainable livelihood** opportunities and promotes **gender empowerment** within the ecological framework of the reserve.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Palamu Tiger Reserve (PTR)**:

• It is located in the **Latehar** and **Palamu** districts of **Jharkhand**.

• It holds historical significance as one of the **first nine tiger reserves** established in India in **1973** under **Project Tiger**.

• The reserve is drained by the **North Koel River** and its tributaries, such as the **Auranga** and **Burha** rivers.

• **Other Tiger Reserves mentioned**:

• **Kanha Tiger Reserve**: Located in **Madhya Pradesh**, it is the first tiger reserve in India to officially introduce a mascot, **Bhoorsingh the Barasingha**.

• **Bandipur Tiger Reserve**: Situated in **Karnataka**, it is a key part of the **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve** and shares borders with Nagarahole and Wayanad.

• **Sundarbans Tiger Reserve**: Found in **West Bengal**, it is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** famous for its **mangrove ecosystem** and the **Royal Bengal Tiger**.
